name: Longto
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 2024. Die Gəmme- und die Vere-Sprachen und das Lɔŋto. Klassensprachen des Samba-Duru am oberen Benue und ihre Beziehungen zum Gur. Ein Bericht. Arbeitspapiere IFEAS 208. Mainz: JGU.
sources.note: Noun-class survey with Lɔŋto data throughout; only prosodic remark is the appendix transcription note that tone is marked (H and clear L marked, M unmarked); Akzent/Betonung/stress/accent = 0 hits.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 2021. 'Lɔ̀ŋto: Tableau de classes nominales [updated]' (handout, Noun class systems in Upper Benue: Samba-Duru, Duru), 1 p.
Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 2018. 'Die "Ding-Klasse" °ne im Lɔŋto und seinen Verwandten'. Slides, Kolloquium R. Kastenholz, JGU Mainz, 2 March 2018, 27 pp.
sources.note: Noun-class morphology only; no tone or stress remarks.

sources.citation: Wikipedia 'Longto language' (refs Ethnologue 18, Kleinewillinghöfer 2012, Westermann & Westermann 2001, ALCAM 2012)
sources.note: Names, villages, classification only; supplied the link to the Mainz dictionary PDF.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid long1387 and reference records 573523, 580704, 310671, 59210, 102156, 312368
sources.note: 0 grammar/phonology/sketch refs for wok; ref 59210 (Hedinger 1987 review of Kuperus, The Londo word) is a Londo (Bantu A.11) item misassigned to wok.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 2022. 'Lɔŋto (aka Voko)'. Adamawa Language Projects web page, JGU Mainz. https://www.blogs.uni-mainz.de/fb07-adamawa/2022/10/16/lɔnto-aka-voko/
sources.note: Sociolinguistic introduction only: 'Lɔŋtɔ has no distinct dialectal areas, although local variants differ in intonation'; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich (avec l'assistance de Illiassou Godje et Bouba Bakary). 2012 [digital edn 2021, 'Dictionnaire lɔŋto ACAD 1.0']. Lexique Lɔ̀ŋtó (~ Voko) - Français. Poli: Lamido de Voko / Comité de Développement du Lamidat de Voko / DFG. 68 pp.
sources.note: Grammatical introduction pp. 3-9 has 1.1 L'alphabet (p. 3) and 1.2 Le ton (p. 4): three tone heights H/M/L plus falling HL and (rarely) ML; TBUs vowels, sometimes l/r and nasals; falling tones only phrase-finally; infinitive tone restriction (2.1). Nothing on stress/accent/prominence ('accent' occurs only as the names of the tone diacritics).

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. [2011]. Die Entwicklung einer Lokativklasse d/r im Samba-Duru (lecture slides, 48 pp.); and: Einfach mal Nein sagen. Negation in drei Adamawasprachen des Norden Kameruns (lecture slides, 22 pp.). JGU Mainz Adamawa project site.
sources.note: Morphology/syntax; tone mentioned only for Beiya and Riitime negation; nothing on Lɔŋto stress.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0, inventory 'longto (GM 1278)', 31 segments, contributors Green & Moran, source 'Kuperus 1985'
sources.note: Inventory lists ˦ ˨ ˦˨ ˨˦ tone segments; its source Kuperus 1985 describes Londo (Bantu), so the inventory is misassigned to Longto; no stress information.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich (avec Bouba Bakary & Illiassou Godje). 2014. Lɔ̀ŋ gɛ̰̀ɛ̰̀dɔ́. Proverbes Lɔ̀ŋtó. Poli, Cameroun.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Tone-marked text collection by the same author; a preface might restate the orthography/tone conventions; not online (listed on the Mainz publications page only).

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 2011. Assoziative Konstruktionen im Vere-Gimme und Lɔŋto, Central Adamawa. In Raija Kramer, Holger Tröbs & Raimund Kastenholz (eds.), Afrikanische Sprachen im Fokus, 143-159. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe.

sources.note: Only peer-reviewed publication with Lɔŋto data; a morphosyntax paper, so at most a footnote on tone, but it is the one place a prosodic preliminary might have been printed.

sources.citation: Westermann, Scott & Annette Westermann. 2001. A Rapid Appraisal Survey of Longto ALCAM [301]: Rapid Appraisal May 2001, Poli Subdivision, Faro Division, North Province, Cameroon. Yaoundé: MINREST/SIL. 12 pp.

sources.note: SIL sociolinguistic survey; unlikely to contain a stress statement but is the only other modern first-hand document on the language (sil.org returned 403; OLAC unreachable).
